construct: A lesion of the medial longitudinal fasciculus interrupts the internuclear projection from the contralateral abducens nucleus to the ipsilateral oculomotor medial-rectus subnucleus, causing ipsilateral adduction weakness with contralateral abducting nystagmus.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: On left gaze, the left abducens nucleus must signal the right medial rectus subnucleus through the right MLF; interruption produces right adduction failure and left abducting nystagmus.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: A right oculomotor fascicular lesion can impair right adduction, but would usually affect additional CN III functions and does not produce the classic ipsilateral adduction deficit plus contralateral abducting nystagmus with preserved convergence.
